reasons: Status is correctly classified as a deviation: Section 8.1 provides only an IP-infringement indemnity expressly stated to be IBM's 'entire obligation', with no prongs for breach of law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, while Section 8.2(a)(3) imposes a broad Customer indemnity for any Services Recipient claim 'related, directly or indirectly, to the Services'.

Redline is actionable and minimal: it adds the three missing IBM indemnity prongs (breach of law, unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) rather than rewriting Section 8.1, reuses the existing notice/control/cooperation conditions in 8.1(a)-(b), and sensibly confines the existing exclusions and the 'entire obligation' sentence to infringement claims so the new prongs are not swallowed by them.

Deletion of the broad Customer indemnity prong 8.2(a)(3) moves toward the preferred position (Customer indemnity limited to Customer content and Customer breach of law) and leaves the surrounding list grammatically intact since the deleted item was not the final enumerated item.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a false negative: IP infringement indemnity already exists in the original Section 8.1, so re-inserting it would not be the smallest edit; the redline correctly builds on it.
Comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, cites the playbook position, and offers the 3x annual charges super-cap fallback.
